name: lib/resilience-core
title: Resilience core
summary: The shared ground of N5: injected time (Clock/Sleep in TS, Runtime in Rust), the config error and validation, stable error codes and the rejection set, and the onEvent hook every primitive takes instead of importing a logger.

ts.name: Sleep
ts.summary: sleep(ms, signal?): rejects with the signal's reason on abort.

ts.name: errorCode
ts.summary: The safe code of any thrown value: its code, else its name, else error; never the message.

ts.name: isRejection
ts.summary: Whether a value's code is a rejection code.

ts.name: ResilienceEvent
ts.summary: {module, type, name?, data?}: codes and numbers only.

ts.name: emit
ts.summary: Calls an onEvent hook; a throwing hook never changes the call.

rs.name: Runtime
rs.summary: now_ms() and sleep(ms): the host's clock and timer.

rs.name: Error
rs.summary: Every way a resilient call fails; Op(E) is the operation's own error.

rs.name: safe_code
rs.summary: A code in the shared alphabet, else error.

behaviour.rule: Time is integer milliseconds; cores take now explicitly; wrappers read an injected clock and sleep.
Config is validated at construction: negative, non-integer or non-finite ms, counts below their minimum, and rates outside [0, 1] are a config error.
An error's code is its stable kebab name; a code that is not in [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]{0,63} becomes error. Messages, URLs and payloads are never recorded (no PII).
circuit-open, bulkhead-full, bulkhead-queue-timeout and rate-limited are rejections: a guard refused the call without running it.
N5 modules import no logger: they take an optional onEvent hook (TS) and return typed errors (Rust).

gaps: Python lands in phase 2 (mzizi-registry#472): a .py sibling, the /v1/py/{name} route in mzizi-api-gateway and a PyPI package.
